findings.text: follow-on: the appended evidence paragraph carries stale suite-arm numbers that the run's own receipts contradict. It states 'Base arm 375241085 with the head test files: 6 failed ... Head arm 2379bb36: 52 passed'. The run's final baseline_suite.log (revision 375241085) reports '7 failed, 45 passed' (failure_count 7 in the manifest's baseline_suite JSON) and after_suite.log reports '53 passed' at c46ccd0768cc6a4a781bafbb959592e7a24434e4, not 2379bb36. The research record's new 'Suite arms' section (docs/research/reference-sign-guard.html) records the same 7/53 figures, so the fragment and the record disagree and the fragment names a head revision the run did not gate. The 6/52 pair belongs to the pre-repair pass the research record explicitly calls earlier. The authoritative numbers are in the logs and manifest; this delivered summary is the odd one out and should carry 7 failed / 53 passed at c46ccd07.

follow-on: the seventeen-slice coverage of done-when (2) is not durably guarded. measure.SLICES is a literal tuple of the seventeen distinct psi grid block starts, but no test asserts its content or length (git grep of the tcv_liuqe_known_answer tests finds SLICES only at its definition and at reference_sign.py:155). A regression that restored the previous twelve hand-chosen indices would drop five grids from the driver and fail no test; the coverage is held only by the one-off receipt reference-sign.log. A test pinning the block starts against a scan of the store, or asserting the driver's outcome row count, would make the clause fail on regression.
